chapter_name: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
learning_objective: 🎯 Decode the ultimate cheat sheet of chemistry: The Periodic Table! Understand how elements are arranged and predict their properties based on their position.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Mendeleev arranged elements by atomic mass and brilliantly left gaps for undiscovered elements. But Moseley fixed the anomalies by proving that properties are actually a periodic function of their Atomic Number, giving us the Modern Periodic Law.

The periodic table is divided into blocks based on which orbital the very last electron enters. The s-block (left) and p-block (right) are representative elements. The d-block (middle) are transition metals, and the f-block (bottom) are inner transition metals.

As you move down a group, atoms get bigger (new shells are added). As you move left to right across a period, atoms actually get SMALLER (more protons pull the same shell closer). Cations (positive) are smaller than their parent atoms, while Anions (negative) are larger.
The energy required to completely remove an electron from a gaseous atom. It generally increases across a period (harder to pull) and decreases down a group (easier to pull from the outer edge).

Electron Gain Enthalpy is the energy released when an atom gains an electron. Electronegativity is an atom's ability to pull shared electrons towards itself in a chemical bond. Fluorine is the most electronegative element!

fun_activity.title: 💥 The Alkali Metal Trend
fun_activity.instructions: If you drop Lithium in water, it fizzes. Sodium catches fire. Potassium explodes instantly! Why? Because as you go DOWN group 1, the ionization enthalpy decreases. The outer electron is further away and easier to lose, making the chemical reaction much more violent!

exam_tips: 📌 Watch out for exceptions in Ionization Enthalpy! Nitrogen has a HIGHER ionization enthalpy than Oxygen because Nitrogen has a stable, exactly half-filled $2p^3$ configuration.

📌 'Isoelectronic species' (ions with the same number of electrons like $O^{2-}, F^-, Na^+, Mg^{2+}$) is a very common question. Among them, the one with the highest positive nuclear charge ($Mg^{2+}$) will have the smallest radius.
📌 Remember that Noble gases have completely positive Electron Gain Enthalpies because their octets are fully satisfied and they do not want to accept an extra electron.
quick_recap: ⭐ The modern periodic table has 7 horizontal rows (Periods) and 18 vertical columns (Groups).
⭐ Metallic character increases down a group and decreases across a period.
⭐ Diagonal relationship: Elements of the second period (like Li, Be) often show similar properties to the elements diagonally below them in the third period (Mg, Al).
